title: Interleaved windowed aggregator with graceful spillover for tenant microbursts
creator: Aisha Patel
body:
Problem: The current real-time metrics pipeline occasionally OOMs or suffers high tail latency during tenant microbursts. Root cause analysis points to unbounded per-tenant window state plus large in-flight aggregation buffers when several tenants simultaneously emit high-cardinality events. Goal: implement an interleaved windowed aggregator that enforces per-tenant memory budgets, preserves low-latency SLOs for hot tenants, and gracefully spills excess state to durable storage with bounded replay cost. The feature should integrate with existing Kafka ingress and the console tracing/alerts we already emit.

This ticket covers design, prototype, unit/integration tests, and a staged rollout (canary -> gradual). The approach must include backpressure signals upstream and clear observability (spill rate, replay latency, per-tenant memory usage).
acceptance_criteria: Per-tenant in-memory state capped and enforced under normal load
Spill-to-disk path triggers when tenant budget exceeded and completes within target time (<= 30s median)
End-to-end p95 ingestion latency does not regress by more than 10% for top 90% tenants under baseline load
System recovers without data loss after spilling and replay; end-to-end counts match within 0.1% after replay
Canary rollout (10% tenants) shows stable metrics for 24h before wider rollout
design_notes: Architecture: place an interleaved aggregator operator between the ingress consumer and windowed aggregator. Each operator slot contains: a) in-memory priority queues per tenant with soft quotas b) per-tenant LRU eviction that pins hot keys c) async spill manager that writes cold tenant windows to local RocksDB then batches to S3 (or object store) for long-term storage.
Memory budgeting: global pool with tenant shares computed from recent 5m throughput and SLA tier. Hot tenants get higher soft quota; every tenant has a hard cap enforced via admission control.

Spill semantics: spill is append-only per-tenant window segment with lightweight index. On spill, we emit a spill-event to a Kafka topic so downstream consumers and the rehydration service can pick up segments for replay. We avoid full rehydration during normal processing; instead we serve misses by on-demand fetch with a small async prefetch window.

Ordering & correctness: maintain event-time windowing by buffering late-arrival markers. We use checkpointed offsets (consumer group + spill offsets) to ensure at-least-once ingestion and idempotent writes when writing aggregates to the downstream materialization store.

Backpressure & admission: when global memory pressure crosses threshold, the operator emits a per-tenant token decrement to the ingress proxy (ingest-proxy) and prioritizes eviction of lower-SLA tenants. We also provide a soft-degrade mode to push best-effort samples for low-priority routes.

Observability: new metrics: ingest.window_spill_rate, ingest.per_tenant_memory_bytes, ingest.rehydrate_latency_ms, ingest.spill_segment_size_bytes. Add dashboards and alerts in console: burst_spill_rate > 5% for > 5m triggers automatic rollback during rollout.
Trade-offs considered: full in-memory retention (fast, but OOM) vs immediate spill (safe, but higher latency). Chosen hybrid reduces tail while preserving fast paths for hot tenants.
Compatibility: reuses existing consumer + checkpointing framework. Minimal contract change: a sink will need to subscribe to 'spill-events' topic for replay and compaction jobs.
tasks: Prototype interleaved aggregator operator and load-test in local cluster (2d)
Implement in-memory tenant quota manager with LRU eviction (3d)
Implement async spill manager (RocksDB local -> S3 batching) and spill-event topic contract (3d)
Integrate backpressure token API with ingest-proxy (2d)
Add observability metrics and dashboards; hook up alerts (2d)
End-to-end integration tests with synthetic microburst harness (2d)
Canary rollout plan + runbook and rollback criteria (1d)
Docs: design doc + runbook + schema for spill-events (1d)
risks: Spill/replay latency may hurt downstream SLAs if many tenants spill simultaneously
Indexing crawl cost for spilled segments could increase read amplification during rehydration
Complexity of admission control may require repeated tuning across cloud regions
Edge cases with late-arrival events and window boundaries require thorough test coverage
rollout_plan: Deploy to staging and run synthetic microburst tests for 48h
Canary: enable for 10% tenants (randomized selection) for 24h, monitor metrics and alerts
Gradual ramp: 10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100% over three days if metrics stable
If spill_rate > 5% for > 30m or rehydrate_90th > 60s, rollback to previous operator
Post-rollout: run compaction job to merge spilled segments and validate aggregates
comments: 2025-01-29 | Liam Chen: initial spike profiling shows three tenants account for 65% of peak memory during the last incident. Prototype will prioritize per-tenant quotas plus LRU keyed retention.
2025-02-02 | Sofia Martinez (PM): please make sure the canary includes a mix of SLA tiers; we must validate both hot enterprise tenants and low-priority trial tenants.
2025-02-05 | DevOps: noted that rolling RocksDB local files needs cleanup hooks tied to Kafka consumer group rebalances. Added a task to ensure safe cleanup on rebalance.
2025-02-08 | Security review (informal): spill-event topic must exclude PII and follow retention policy. We will apply transform pipeline before spill write if needed.

2025-02-12 | Liam Chen: implemented basic spill manager and end-to-end integration tests passing on staging. Observed median rehydrate latency of 4.8s; p95 at 14s for synthetic worst-case. Will tune batch sizes and prefetch heuristics next.
